correctness.rationale: After scaling to \(a=1/2\), the essential threshold is \(1\). For the proposed disk center \(c=(73/100,73/100)\) and radius \(R=481/200\), direct recomputation of the spiral-distance function gives a minimum near \(\theta=\pi\) with squared distance about \(5.82656\), safely above \(R^2=5.784025\); the package's outward interval argument covers the entire continuum \([3.1415,7]\), and the reverse triangle inequality covers \(\theta\ge7\). The exact alternating Bessel series has the order-six partial sum negative and a decreasing alternating tail beginning negative, so \(J_0(R)<0\), hence \(j_{0,1}<R\). A disk-supported Dirichlet ground-state trial function therefore has Rayleigh quotient below the known essential threshold, forcing discrete spectrum. Inclusion of cut spirals extends the same disk from \(\beta=\pi\) to all \(\beta>\pi\).
residual_risks: The constant \(\pi\) is only a sufficient bound and is far above the numerically indicated onset near \(1.43\).

The later Barseghyan–Exner paper studies Lieb–Thirring estimates for shrinking spirals rather than this cut-cavity optimization. Resultary returned no earlier implication-equivalent half-turn theorem.
